text.mountains_poem.alpha: §l§a[Mountains Poem]§r§l§2 You are currently running the §b§nPublic Beta Test Version.§r§l§2 If you encounter any bugs, please contact us and provide the crash log so we can fix the mod. （。＾▽＾）
text.mountains_poem.alpha.hover: Open the MCMod page to report issues
book.mountains_poem.mountains_book.entry: North lies snow and taiga; south, peach blossom and bamboo. The green-rock mountains hide zheng, and the blood-stained land waits beneath the Under.$(br2)Yan and old-growth yan forests yield yan fruit; jiang wood is tough; shatang, pan, peach, jianmei bamboo and huang_guan each have their own gifts.$(br2)Green-rock mountains are rich in green rock and zheng; the dark taiga belongs to ao yin.
$(li)Food and torches.$(li)An iron or blood-copper sword.$(li)Jade and blood-copper plates for trade and rites.$(li)A bed; beds work in the Under.$(li)Milk, for plague and foul odours.
Rice, yan fruit, shatang fruit and meat all stave off hunger.$(br2)Boil rice; roast raw meat. In snow, carry a bowl of hot soup.$(br2)Salt preserves food and gives meat sauce more flavour.
After dusk, ghosts wander the dark.$(br2)Build a house with a door, then light torches. Ghosts fear light and burn in daylight.$(br2)If you hear a hanged ghost's rope, do not look back.
A bowl of hot rice is the plainest comfort in this land.$(br2)Eat it when hungry; it restores a good deal of hunger.

You wake as wind runs through the yan forest. Birds call, and something unknown roars far away.$(br2)This is the Classic of Mountains and Seas reflected in another time: nine-tailed foxes in snow, xuan tortoises in river bends, mountain gods listening to prayers at their altars.$(br2)This Classic of Mountains and Seas will walk with you through your first days.

$(li)Qingqiu: food, shelter and travel.$(li)Living things: beasts, birds, ghosts and gods.$(li)Plants and stone: woods, crops and ores.$(li)Crafts: blood copper, bronze, jade and paper.$(li)Rites: jade offerings and the blessings of the gods.$(li)The Under: another world beneath the yellow springs.$(br2)Pages link to one another; follow the links when a name is strange.
Mountain weather turns without warning.$(br2)Store torches before rain and firewood before snow; if you hear a baby cry, look up for a gu eagle.$(br2)Travel safely.

Forged from blood-copper plates, the blade fears no fire.$(br2)It sets the undead alight and weakens the living.$(br2)Blood-copper tools last long but are hard to repair; once ruined, they must be reforged.

Axes, picks, shovels, hoes, ge and yue are all made from blood-copper plates.$(br2)Smithing templates upgrade copper weapons to blood copper; blood-copper armour turns heavy blows.$(br2)Blood-copper weapons do not burn, which is more than iron can say.
Copper ingots, netherite scrap and blood copper yield a blood-copper ingot.
A smithing template upgrades copper weapons to blood copper.
The bronze dou is a ritual vessel for meat sauce.$(br2)Bronze vessels include the dou, gui, zun, jue, yue and small ding; they are both tableware and altar ware.

A bronze gui holds sixty-four portions of rice and is the great vessel of mountain sacrifices; a jue holds water, milk or juice; a zun holds wine or soup.$(br2)Wrought patterns dress the bronze; the finer the pattern, the better the gods like it.$(br2)A yue can serve as a weapon, and a small ding can boil meat.
The dou is forged from copper ingots and a wrought pattern; it is made for meat sauce.
The gui is the great vessel of sacrifice and holds a great deal of rice.
The nine-tailed fox hanfu comes in bamboo green, mugwort green, peach red and jun black.$(br2)Cut from cloth and fox fur, it is light and beautiful.

White fox and ao yin fur coats are thicker and suit the snow.$(br2)Hanfu can be ceremonial dress or light armour; it is more presentable before a god than plate.$(br2)Fox fur, ao yin fur and cloth are the three main materials.
Jade paste is the essence of jade and water; it can be medicine or offering.$(br2)Jade comes as green jade, white jade, jinyu and broken jade; broken jade can still be carved.

The jade carver is the jade-worker's station; pendants, tablets, rings and ornaments take shape there.$(br2)Jade is the offering the mountain gods know best; one good piece is worth a thousand words.$(br2)Jade-mason villagers will trade jade work with you.
The jade carver is built from wood and stone, and is the jade-worker's livelihood.
Jade paste can be bucketed and carried with you.
A mooncake is pastry wrapped around filling and baked.$(br2)Egg yolk, fruit, honey, ginger and centipede can all go inside.

Unbaked mooncakes go into a furnace or smoker until golden.$(br2)Ancient five-nut, dark cuisine, eternal heart, sanguine and under-flower are a few special mooncakes.$(br2)Mooncakes keep well and travel well.
Mooncake pastry is the foundation of every mooncake.
Wrap the filling, and it is ready for the oven.

Pour pulp into the papermaking board, lift it with a bamboo or wooden mesh, and set it on the drying rack.$(br2)When it is dry, you have a sheet of paper.$(br2)Paper binds books and makes totem scrolls.
The papermaking board is the first stop in making paper.
The bamboo mesh lifts the pulp; its weave is fine and close.
The drying rack lets wet paper dry slowly and evenly.
Carve the likeness of a living thing into a xuan shell, and it becomes an engraved shell.$(br2)Different patterns answer to different totems.

Xuan shells can be carved into totem scrolls; a totem records the name of a living thing and serves in rites and prayers.$(br2)Battle shells can guard their bearer in danger.$(br2)Carnelian, zheng saliva or an engraved shell, joined with a blank scroll, makes a totem.
One engraved shell and one blank scroll make a Zheng totem.
Health 80, attack 14.$(br2)It haunts the dark taiga, its pelt black as ink, its claws cold and bright.

The Shen Yi Jing tells of a beast called ao yin in the western wilds, waiting for those who walk alone.$(br2)It fears neither fire nor potions; those near it fall into madness, seeing only chaos and the urge to kill.$(br2)Its claws shake the ground, and even those ten paces away lose their footing.$(br2)Fight it with bow and crossbow at range; if it closes, retreat and wait for another opening.
Ao yin keeps to hidden paths; its pelt is rarely taken.$(br2)Hunters say it leaves scorch marks but seldom a whole corpse.$(br2)If you only wish to see it from afar, stand upwind.

The Classic of Mountains and Seas has a bird called shang fu: like a chicken, with three heads, six eyes, six wings and three feet; eating it ends sleep.$(br2)Health 45, attack 3; it paces the plains and snowy plains.$(br2)Its feathers make arrows, though its meat is scant.

In the Classic of the Southern Mountains, Mount Ji has a beast called bo yi: like a sheep, with nine tails and four ears, its eyes on its back; wearing its image banishes fear.$(br2)Health 20, attack 3; it eats xun-leaf berries.$(br2)Its hide is soft and often used as lining.

The xian goat comes from Mount Qianlai in the Classic of the Western Mountains: like a sheep with a horse's tail; health 60, attack 3.$(br2)Shan gao is an old book's pig-shaped beast, fond of cursing; health 20, attack 2, and its abuse carries far.$(br2)The zhi is the man-eater of Mount Fuyu in the Classic of the Southern Mountains: health 60, attack 3; it is like a tiger with a cow's tail.
Health 30, attack 5.$(br2)It looks like a beast stepped down from a bronze vessel, its body furred with verdigris.

The beast-mask pattern on a bronze vessel came alive at some hour.$(br2)It oxidises with time: first mottled, then rusted; wax preserves its sheen.$(br2)It pulls down bronze statues and guards bronze vessels.$(br2)Feed it copper, and perhaps it will warm to you.
Bronze fragments and monster-statue fragments.$(br2)The fragments can be recast or made into armour.
Health 130, attack 18.$(br2)A huge ox with a white head, one eye and a snake's tail. Where it walks, grass and trees die.

The Classic of the Eastern Mountains tells of Mount Tai's fei: it drains water, kills grass, and its coming brings a great plague.$(br2)It spits plague balls and carries pestilence; those near it sicken, and those it gores sicken too.$(br2)It breaks wooden doors, fears neither fire nor potions, and will not follow you across dimensions.$(br2)Carry milk and potions, and do not linger downwind.
Its horn makes the Plague Horn, whose note scatters pestilence.$(br2)Bone, sinew and bile can also be used in medicine, but handle them with care.
Health 50, attack 10.$(br2)When it spreads its wings, its feathers open like evening clouds.

The Classic of the Southern Mountains tells of the fenghuang of Mount Dan: like a chicken, five-coloured and patterned; the head is virtue, the wings duty, the back propriety, the breast benevolence, the belly trust.$(br2)Health 50, attack 10; proud, and slow to bow.$(br2)Feed it jinyu jade or dan fruit, and it may accept you; once tamed, it drives off evil.
The fenghuang seldom leaves a feather; where it flies, a faint light remains.$(br2)If it is close to you, it will come down in your hour of need.

When the sun sets, ghosts come out of the shadows.$(br2)All fear light and burn by day; all give way to mountain gods and the dragon-headed god.$(br2)The blood-stained land and the Under's wilds are where they gather.

Hanged ghost: health 40, attack 3. It casts a rope of resentment; those struck fall into madness.$(br2)Wandering ghost: health 40, attack 2. It roams the wilds, opens doors and flees in panic.$(br2)Under ghost: health 40, attack 2. Common in the Under, and comes in groups.$(br2)Examination ghost: health 45, attack 4. It opens doors, panics, and hunts at night.
Offer a Bottle of Soul Shards at the altar to draw one of the ghosts.$(br2)If you want no trouble, be home before sunrise.$(br2)If a hanged ghost's rope catches you, break free first, then strike.
Health 30, attack 8.$(br2)It circles high overhead, crying like an infant.

The Classic of the Southern Mountains tells of Mount Lu Wu's gu eagle: like an eagle with horns, its voice a baby's, and it eats people.$(br2)It stoops to strike, its feathers hard as iron.$(br2)If you hear a baby cry and see no child, look up.
Its feathers make arrow fletching, and its bones can be used in medicine.$(br2)Its meat is sour and bitter, unfit for the table.
Health 80, attack 3.$(br2)It glides over the water weeds, swift as a shadow.

The Classic of the Central Mountains tells of Yang Mountain's hua she: human face, jackal body, bird wings, moving like a snake; its coming foretells a great flood.$(br2)It loves water and moves very fast, but seldom attacks.$(br2)If you see it hurry through the wood, seek higher ground.
Hua she seldom stays; it is hard to see clearly.$(br2)Where it passes, the water's edge is left slick.
Health 10, attack 3.$(br2)It is small, but always digging in the earth.

The hun of old books loves to search the soil.$(br2)Feed it a rong grass tuber and it will take you as its master; lead it to bare earth and it may dig up something long buried.$(br2)It is timid, and runs first when danger comes.
What it digs up varies: broken jade, old copper.$(br2)Be patient; there is always something.
Health 30, attack 3.$(br2)It crouches in the branches with a stone in its hand.

The Classic of the Western Mountains tells of Mount Chongwu's jufu: like a monkey with patterned arms, and skilled at throwing.$(br2)It does not rush you; it throws from afar, and a struck stone only angers it.$(br2)Jufu gather in bands; do not stand long under their trees.
Its humerus makes a long-handled weapon, hard at the joint and whistling when swung.$(br2)Its hide is usable, though it smells.
Health 50, attack 6.$(br2)It is like a raccoon with a mane, both male and female, and gentle in temper.

The Classic of the Southern Mountains tells of Mount Dan Yuan's lei: like a raccoon with a mane, both male and female; eating it cures jealousy.$(br2)It eats beef, and can be tamed by feeding; once tame it follows its master and guards the house.$(br2)Its mane is soft and often made into ornaments.
Lei meat is edible, and its mane makes ornaments.$(br2)It dislikes fighting and hides when danger comes.
Health 46, attack 0.$(br2)It is like a horse, white-headed and red-tailed, and its call is like a song.

The Classic of the Southern Mountains tells of Mount Niu Yang's lu shu: wearing its image is good for descendants.$(br2)It never attacks, and likes to walk the plains and yan forest.$(br2)Its hide is soft and tough, good for robes and offerings.
Lu shu hide is soft and tough, good for clothing and rites.$(br2)It dislikes fighting; take it in one clean blow.
Health 25, attack 3.$(br2)In the snowy plains and slopes, a red tail sometimes slips past.

The Classic of the Southern Mountains tells of Qingqiu's fox: nine tails, a voice like a baby's, and it eats people; whoever eats it is not poisoned.$(br2)It does not attack unprovoked, but chases lei and pigs.$(br2)Feed it sweet berries to win its trust; once tamed it follows you and strikes at your enemies.$(br2)It is suspicious by nature; do not swing a sword in front of it.
Its pelt is nearly invisible in snow.$(br2)If you treat it well, it will warm your hands on a snowy night.
Health 40, attack 4.$(br2)It lifts its head from the river bend, water still dripping from its mane.

The Classic of the Northern Mountains tells of the water horse: like a horse with a cow's tail, able to walk in water.$(br2)It eats golden apples, and once fed it can be tamed; a tamed water horse carries its rider across water and wears water-horse armour.$(br2)It sometimes charges those on the bank; being struck is no joke.
Its mane makes reins and ornaments.$(br2)With blood-copper water-horse armour, it moves steadily through deep water.
Health 30, attack 18.$(br2)Deep in the yan forest, the white ape moves through the canopy like wind.

In the Wu Yue Chun Qiu, the woman of Yue met a white ape and understood the sword.$(br2)It is gentle until struck; then it speeds in, its fist heavy as a mountain.$(br2)It loves yan fruit and golden yan fruit, and will accept food; but if you come empty-handed, step back three paces.
White ape meat is edible; its nails and climbing claws make a climbing hook.$(br2)With a hook, no tree is too high.
Health 24, attack 4.$(br2)In river bends and shallows, the xuan tortoise swims slowly under its heavy shell.

The Classic of the Southern Mountains tells of Mount Niu Yang's xuan tortoise: a bird's head and a viper's tail; wearing it prevents deafness.$(br2)It is gentle, and pulls into its shell when startled.$(br2)Feed it crimson fungus or cold crimson fungus salad, and it grants the blessing of the Nocturnal Journeyman.$(br2)Its scales and the crimson xuan tortoise's shell are good for armour and ritual ware.
Health 30, attack 5.$(br2)It lives in the crimson forest, livelier than the common xuan tortoise, and more willing to follow a person.$(br2)Feed it crimson fungus, and it will take you as its master.
A shell shed by the xuan tortoise kin, hard and warm.$(br2)It can be carved into armour or into a totem.
Health 50, attack 11.$(br2)In the green-rock mountains, a red-leopard shadow flickers past.

The Classic of the Western Mountains tells of Mount Zhang E's zheng: like a red leopard, five tails, one horn, its voice like striking stone.$(br2)It carries a sharp odour; those near it glow and slow.$(br2)Catch its saliva in a glass bottle to make a strange syrup.$(br2)It does not fear people, but dislikes being stared at.
Zheng saliva makes syrup; catch it in a glass bottle.$(br2)Its pelt is marked with red, but is hard to take whole.

Rice is the staple of this land.$(br2)It is mostly found in the chests of old houses, sacrificial halls and ancient graves; it is hard-won, so waste none.$(br2)Rice is also a chief offering: a bronze gui is often filled with sixty-four portions.

Big carrots, scallions, ginger, garlic, ting zhu, zhu yu and rong grass are common at the table.$(br2)Salt comes from salt ore and salt blocks, preserves food, and ting zhu and zhu yu juices are fine seasonings.$(br2)Fruit and meat come from the woods and hills.
A bowl of hot rice, with meat sauce or pickles, is a good meal.

Jade ore lies underground; green jade, white jade, inferior jade and jinyu each have their uses.$(br2)Blood copper is found in mountains and deep stone; blood-copper plates make weapons and armour.$(br2)Carnelian and salt are also found in the wild; the green-rock mountains yield green rock for building.
Beneath the Under lies under-iron, a metal of another world, hard and heavy.$(br2)It is found in the under-rock hills and the Under's ruins, deep and hard to mine.
An ingot smelted from copper, netherite scrap and blood copper, heavy and rust-red.

Yan grows in the yan forest and old-growth yan forest, and bears yan fruit among its leaves.$(br2)Yan fruit is sweet-sour; golden yan fruit is rarer, and the white ape prizes both.$(br2)Yan wood is light and tough, good for furniture and bows.

Jiang wood is hard, good for boats and building; shatang forest is rich in shatang fruit; peach forest in peach blossom and peach wood.$(br2)Pan forest, jianmei bamboo jungle and huang_guan forest each have their own trees.$(br2)Jianmei bamboo makes bamboo ware; huang_guan wood carries a faint medicinal scent.
Fruit of the yan tree, sweet-sour and full of juice.$(br2)White apes and jufu both love it.

Pestilence: plague gnaws at life.$(br2)Madness: the mind scatters and limbs slow.$(br2)Resentment of the Southern Mountains God: resentment enters the body and wastes it.$(br2)Lush: green life wells up.$(br2)Nocturnal Journeyman: night vision, speed and jumping.$(br2)Dehydration: thirst cuts like a blade.$(br2)Lost souls, evil qi, chaos and strong odour are all misery.$(br2)Gu-resistance, hydrated skin and the Mountain God's Blessing drive such things away.

Soul Strength: a boot enchantment that lightens the step.$(br2)Tight: a chest enchantment that turns points aside.$(br2)Control of Water Horses: a weapon enchantment, named for the old saying.$(br2)Rock Attached: a weapon enchantment that makes blows heavier.
Xuan shells and totem scrolls are another protection.$(br2)Different patterns answer to different living things; in danger, they lend their strength.

The Southern Mountain pendant, the Second Southern Mountain pendant and the Ninth Central Mountain pendant answer to three gods.$(br2)They can be found in ruins, bought from jade masons, or received in rites.$(br2)The jade is warm, and grows warmer in the hand.

Spread the white jian grass mat on the altar; bury a hollow mud brick below, and place in it three portions of fowl or beast meat (at least sixteen each), a jade tablet and a xuan shell; above, set a bronze gui filled with sixty-four portions of rice.$(br2)Hold a sword or jade tablet in the main hand and the matching pendant in the off hand to call the god.$(br2)When lightning falls, the god stands upon the altar.

Once the god has come, offer different xuan shells to reveal different divine aspects; each aspect grants a different blessing.$(br2)Strength, speed, health, absorption, jumping, abundance and lushness are all gifts of the mountain gods.$(br2)Come empty-handed, and you will face only their wrath.
Health 200, attack 22.$(br2)Horse body, dragon head, walking on clouds.

The Classic of the Central Mountains tells of a mountain god with a horse's body and a dragon's head.$(br2)It eats golden apples and can be tamed slowly; once tame it follows you and attacks monsters.$(br2)Its temper is not bad, but its patience is short; feed it until it is satisfied.
A tamed dragon-headed god stays by its master and charges any monster it sees.$(br2)It does not speak, but gives a low call when you are hurt.
Health 180, attack 32.$(br2)Its aspect is younger, but its lightning is just as sharp.

The mountain god of the Second Southern Classic in the Classic of Mountains and Seas.$(br2)It is a little less imposing than the South Mountain God, but no less proud; it too sends resentment and grants blessings.$(br2)Call it with the matching pendant and offer well, and it will remember your name.
Jade tablets are carved at the jade carver; they feel cool in the hand.

Hold a jade tablet in the main hand and lu shu hide in the off hand, and sweep the air: lightning falls, and the Heart of Lu Shu may come with it.$(br2)With a battle xuan shell in the off hand instead, the lightning turns into strength, speed and resistance.$(br2)The jade tablet wears with use; a rite is no game, so do not perform it indoors.
One who receives the Heart of Lu Shu feels their pulse like a drum and their step grow light.$(br2)The blessing does not last, but it is enough to carry you out of danger.
Health 280, attack 35.$(br2)Upon the altar, the mountain god wears moss and lightning.

The mountain god of the southern classics in the Classic of Mountains and Seas.$(br2)It is wrapped in the Resentment of the Southern Mountains God; those near it are eaten by resentment, and it fears neither fire, potions, falling nor cactus.$(br2)It has several aspects, changing with the xuan shell offered; each aspect grants strength, speed, health, absorption, jumping, abundance or lushness.

Lay the white jian grass mat, hollow mud brick, bronze gui and rice on the altar, and hold the sacrificial sword and the Southern Mountain pendant to call it down.$(br2)The full rite is described in the Rite of the Mountain Gods.
Built of wood and stone, the altar is the workstation of the Huaxia sorcerer.$(br2)Where there is a Huaxia sorcerer in a village, there is usually an altar.

Spread the white jian grass mat on the altar to begin a rite.$(br2)A hollow mud brick can be buried below; a bronze gui can be set above.$(br2)Where there is a Huaxia sorcerer in a village, an altar is rarely far away.

Sanguine Desert: red sand and sanguine cactus.$(br2)Sanguine Valley: blood-red soil and thorns.$(br2)Ancient Battlefields: under grass and old soldiers.$(br2)Under-Rock Hills: under rock and ore.$(br2)Under Wastes: barren and wide.

Under ghosts, hanged ghosts, wandering ghosts and examination ghosts roam the dark; sanguine plants cut those who come near.$(br2)Night in the Under is colder than in the overworld.$(br2)If you lose your way, follow the high ground of the under-rock hills; ruins can often be seen from there.
The death jade token is made from blood-thorn, a bottle of soul shards and a tally; durability 64.

Build a frame of under-rock bricks at least two wide and three high (at most twenty-one).$(br2)Hold the death jade token and right-click inside the frame; a purple gate lights.$(br2)Step through, and you are in the Under.

The Under has no sky; bedrock is overhead, and the air holds moisture and dust.$(br2)Beds still work; bring torches, food and weapons.$(br2)The death jade token wears with each opening; carry several.

Ancient ruins lie in the Under: abandoned houses, old graves, a broken ghost village, sacrificial halls and five kinds of under-ruin.$(br2)Chests may hold jade, blood copper, under-iron and old scrolls.$(br2)Some ruins keep guardian beasts that still obey a thousand-year-old law.

Take torches and a weapon; do not go deep alone.$(br2)Most bronze in a sacrificial hall still works; best not to open the coffins in old graves.$(br2)Rows of under-rock bricks mean a larger building is near.
Heavy, cold, and very tough.$(br2)Four under-iron pieces and two netherite ingots make one under-iron ingot.
Under-iron makes swords and armour; the armour turns the heaviest blows.
Under-iron comes from the Under's ore veins and ruins.$(br2)It is heavier than blood copper; mind the heat when forging.
book.mountains_poem.mountains_book.name: Classic of Mountains and Seas
book.mountains_poem.mountains_book.landi: Here are the mountains and seas of the Classic, reflected in another time.$(br2)Within these pages live its beasts, plants, crafts and rites.$(br2)Read it before you step through the gate.$(br2)$(o)—Ode to Qingqiu
